newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Bank of Canada seen cutting rates again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank of Canada seen cutting rates again.

text.p: The Bank of Canada is likely to cut domestic interest rates further this month, although they are already at their lowest levels in almost four decades, economists and money market traders said on Monday.

Analysts said a strengthening Canadian dollar, continued signs of economic weakness and the likelihood that the U.S. Federal Reserve will not raise rates this year are the factors pointing to another rate cut.

"It's just a question of strategy, what day they feel may be best at this point. Given where the currency is I think they've pretty much made up their mind that they'll go," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.

Canada's central bank has already cut short-term interest rates 10 times this year to try to spur economic growth. The bank has cut rates by a total of 475 basis points since May 1995. A basis point is one one-hundreth of a percentage point.

In October alone, the Bank of Canada lowered its key bank rate three times, bringing it to a 33-year low of 3.5 percent. The bank rate is similar to the U.S. Federal funds rate in that both are seen as benchmarks of short-term rates.

However, the flurry of rate cuts this year has had little impact so far in stimulating economic growth. An economic report issued on Monday showed the value of Canadian building permits issued in September fell 3.4 percent, against forcasts of a 3.6 percent rise.
Expectations that the Bank of Canada will again reduce rates in a bid to stimulate growth returned to the market last week.

Canadian treasury bill traders began betting on a rate cut after U.S. economic data prompted forecasts that the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate setting committee will leave rates unchanged when it meets on November 13.
The likelihood that the Fed will remain on hold is seen by many traders as providing an opportunity for the Bank of Canada to ease further.

"It (a rate cut) is pretty much priced in. I think it is a sure thing almost, as much as it could be," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "Anything to get the economy stimulated is needed right now."

Analysts said the key to another rate cut is the strength of the Canadian dollar. The currency on Friday reached its strongest levels so far this year, firming past the key C$1.3333 (US$0.7500) level. As recently as September 6, it was C$1.3729 (US$0.7284).

In making its three most recent cuts, the Canidian central bank has cited its desire to offset the impact of a stronger Canadian dollar on the economy. The bank sees a stronger dollar as having the same impact as higher interest rates because it reduces the competitiveness of Canadian exports.

"The triggerpoint is likely to be if the Canadian dollar rises from these levels and sustains itself at a higher value," said Barry Davenport, senior vice-president of treasury with Bank of Canada. Davenport said a rate cut is most likely if the dollar strengthens past C$1.3325 (US$0.7505).

Analysts said a Statistics Canada report on October employment due out on Friday could also play a key role in the timing of another Bank of Canada rate cut. The Bank of Canada last month cut rates just days after a similar report showed higher-than-expected unemployment in September.
